alerts.reason: Intentional JavaScriptCore evaluation of the fixed generated pixoo-baked.generated.js application-bundle resource. Production constructs the renderer without an injected source; the source override is used by a standalone regression fixture only. Peer state is bounded JSON passed as function arguments and parsed as data, never concatenated into evaluated source. The context exposes no native file/network callbacks or remote script-loading route. Existing bundled-renderer/cache/activity/bounds and cross-language pixel-parity tests exercise this boundary. This is a source trust-policy review, not proof against maliciously replaced application code.

Remove API-key writes to UserDefaults. Shipped sandbox macOS/iOS apps use noninteractive device-local Keychain storage; migration acknowledges secure persistence before removing legacy defaults/profile copies. Empty secure tombstones prevent stale profile resurrection, and unavailable secure storage never falls back to plaintext for provider requests. Unsandboxed development retains the explicit Node CLI JSON contract with exclusive atomic 0600 writes. Injected migration/provider-resolution regressions cover failure and clear/restart; real Keychain access and shipped-client acceptance were not performed.

Pin the monitor-service wake executable to /system/bin/input, with fixed keyevent arguments; do not resolve an executable through PATH. Android compile/unit tests pass; no device power or shared service state changed.

Pin the Android wake input executable to /system/bin/input while preserving argument-array execution and existing wake-lock fallback. Android compile/unit tests pass; physical device wake acceptance remains separate.

Replace saved/discovered full-URL debug logging with the canonical host/port endpoint projection. Token query, URL user-info and path are not included. Android compile and 577 unit tests pass; no real paired URL or logcat secrets were collected.

The official GitHub updater retains standard CA/hostname checks using patched OkHttp 4.12.1, and independently verifies the downloaded APK signer against the installed application. Leaf-certificate pinning of rotating GitHub certificates is not the chosen trust policy. This does not claim that TLS or supply-chain attacks are impossible.

Pairing connects to the user-selected daemon. No permissive trust manager or hostname verifier was introduced; standard TLS verification applies to HTTPS endpoints. The product has no pre-established certificate for every self-hosted daemon. Certificate enrollment/rotation requires a separate protocol decision. Pairing on plain HTTP has a transport-confidentiality limitation.

User-configured daemon endpoint, not a single vendor HTTPS service. Standard OkHttp certificate and hostname verification is retained for TLS. Hardcoding a vendor certificate would break self-hosted endpoints and is not an authentication fix for intentional plain LAN ws/http. Pairing authorization and transport confidentiality are distinct; unencrypted LAN transport remains a limitation.

Intentional user-confirmed updater. Its only current UI caller receives an app-owned cache file from the bounded downloader, which verifies the official release asset URL, SHA-256/size, exact package name, newer version code, and a nonempty signer set equal to the installed app before returning it. The system installer still requires user approval. Static source and existing updater regressions reviewed; no arbitrary downloaded APK was installed.

Disable manifest backup and explicitly exclude all app storage domains from legacy backup, Android 12+ cloud backup and device transfer. Packaged-manifest/resource regression and 577 Android unit tests pass. OEM physical backup/restore is not tested.

This is a new default-branch fingerprint of the reviewed /sse admission path. Authentication and the global 200-request/second counter precede the handler; at most 16 SSE clients/timers exist. Actual loopback capacity/recovery tests passed. The earlier fingerprint #47 was individually reviewed; this new ID remains open pending approval.
